rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: Rūḥ al-Maʿānī defines guardianship as preservation and rectification, noting that the root originally referred to protecting livestock by feeding it or warding off predators.
rows.anchor: وجاء في (روح المعاني) تفسير (راعون) : "قائمون بحفظها وإصلاحها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says riyāʿa is broader than mere preservation: it includes care, correction, stewardship, and monitoring, all needed to discharge a trust.
rows.anchor: فالرعي ليس مجرد الحفظ؛ بل هو الحِفْظُ والإصلاح والعناية بالأمر وتولي شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A trusted guardian must attend to dependents’ needs, a ruler must oversee subjects, and one entrusted with crops, livestock, or religious obligations must actively discharge the charge and seek what pleases God.
rows.anchor: فمن ائتمن عندك أهله وصغاره، فلا بد من أن تتفقد أمورهم وتنظر في أحوالهم وحاجاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike chastity, which remains with the person, trusts may be remote or hidden from view and exposed to thieves, so the trustee must inspect and tend them like a shepherd; riyāʿa is the apt term.
rows.anchor: فهي تحتاج إلى تفقد ورعاية كما يحتاج الحيوان إلى حفظه من الذئاب والوحوش الضارية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal form raaʿūn, rather than the verb yarʿawn, signals that this guardianship must remain constant and never lapse.
rows.anchor: لم يقل: (يرعون) ذلك ليدلَّ على لزوم ثبات الرعي ودوامه وعدم الإخلال به البتة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people received clear messengers, mocked them, persisted in shirk, and only professed faith when punishment arrived; that late faith did not benefit them.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر أن أممهم استهزؤوا برسلهم وبقوا على شركهم حتى رأوا بأس الله ينزل بهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To compare the Qurʾānic uses of jāʾa and atā, the author cautions against extracting a phrase: read each entire verse and its context, including the differing accounts of the Hour in 6:31 and 6:40–41.
rows.anchor: لا يصح اقتطاع جزء من الآية للاستدلال، بل ينبغي النظرُ في الآية كلها وفي السياق أيضاً ليصحَّ الاستدلالُ والحكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasas uses the command usluk for Moses’ hand because the story repeatedly has people traverse places and paths, while Naml omits the travel episodes and starts with Moses speaking to his family at the fire.
rows.anchor: ذلك لأنه تردد سلوكُ الأمكنةِ والسبل في قصة موسى في القصص، بخلاف ما ورد في النمل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qasas narrative recounts the chest traveling to Pharaoh’s palace, the sister tracking Moses, Moses’ flight to Midian, his route to the righteous man, and his return journey; this makes its language of traversing apt.
rows.anchor: فقد ورد فيها، أي: في سورة القصص سلوك الصندوق بموسى، وهو مُلقى في اليمّ إلى قصر فرعون، وسلوك أخته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb dakhal and its derivatives occur five times in Naml but not in Qasas, another reason the author gives for using adkhil in Naml and usluk in Qasas.
rows.anchor: الفعل (دخل) ومشتقاته تكرر خمس مرات في النمل في حين، لم يرد هذا الفعل ولا شيء من مشتقاته في القصص،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idkhāl is more specific than sulūk: sulūk can mean entering, but it can also mean traveling along a road or through a place.
rows.anchor: إن الإدخال أخص من السَّلْك أو السلوك اللذين هما مصدر الفعل سلك، لأن السَّلْك أو السلوك، قد يكون إدخالاً وغير إدخال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrection statement in al-Muʾminūn fits its opening praise of believers, since belief in resurrection is integral to faith, and its closing question about creation in vain and return to God.
rows.anchor: ومن لوازم الإيمان، الإيمانُ بالبعث، وناسب قوله في آخر السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that people will dispute before their Lord fits al-Zumar’s opening about revelation and God judging their disagreements, as well as its ending where judgment is completed in truth; disputes require a judgment between parties.
rows.anchor: فإن الخصومة تقتضي حكمًا بين المتخاصمين، كما ناسب قوله تعالى في خاتمة السورة: {وَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zumar singles out the Prophet from the others and presents them as multiple sides because dispute and judgment require more than one party.
rows.anchor: فأفردَ النبيَّ عنهم، وجعلهم فريقين، ذلك لأن الخصومة والفصل يقتضيان أكثر من طرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muʾminūn uses one collective group for resurrection because everyone is raised and the passage discusses humanity’s creation, development, death, and resurrection generally.
rows.anchor: فقال: {ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ يَوْمَ القيامة تُبْعَثُونَ} بجعلهم فريقاً واحداً، إذ كلهم يُبعثون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited observation contrasts a healthy wealthy person who withholds beneficence with the same person when ill, who panics and begins making bequests.
rows.anchor: إذا صَحَّ الغنيُّ مَنَعَ المعروف وشَحَّ بماله، وإذا مرض جزع وأخذ يوصي

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr says harm makes a person panic, feel terror, and despair of future good, while a blessing makes him withhold from others and refuse God’s due from it.
rows.anchor: وجاء في (تفسير ابن كثير) : "أي: إذا مَسَّهُ الضُّرُّ فَزِعَ وجزع

rows.speaker: فتح القدير
rows.claim: Fatḥ al-Qadīr, citing al-Ṣiḥāḥ, glosses halūʿ as extreme greed and the worst, most excessive panic; calamity yields much panic and prosperity yields much withholding.
rows.anchor: وجاء في (فتح القدير) : "قال في الصحاح: الهلع في اللغة: أَشَدُّ الحرص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jazaʿ is the opposite of patience, as shown by the Qurʾānic pairing of whether people panic or remain patient in 14:21.
rows.anchor: والجزع ضد الصبر ونقيضه، وقد قابله الله بالصبر فقال: {سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْنَآ أَجَزِعْنَآ أَمْ صَبَرْنَا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage puts harm before good because the sūra opens with a demand for punishment and has just depicted the criminal’s wish to ransom himself and the blaze that tears at the skin.
rows.anchor: وقد بدأ بالشر قبل الخير، فقال: {إِذَا مَسَّهُ الشر جَزُوعاً * وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ الخير مَنُوعاً} وذلك لأن السياق يقتضي ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ promise to bring news from the fire corresponds to Qasas’s closing promise that God will show signs, with a deliberate verbal echo between saʾātīkum and sayurīkum.
rows.anchor: ومناسبته لقوله تعالى في آخر السورة: {الحمد للَّهِ سَيُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ فَتَعْرِفُونَهَا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml repeats the verb of coming while Qasas uses it once; the author reads the repetition as confidence and strength, fitting Naml, and the single use as fitting Qasas’s fearful atmosphere.
rows.anchor: فأكد الإتيان في سورة النمل لقوة يقينه وثقته بنفسه، والتوكيد يدل على القوة، في حين لم يكرر فعل الإتيان في القصص مناسبة لجو الخوف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated wording also fits the narrative counts: the verb atā occurs twelve times in Naml and six times in Qasas.
rows.anchor: إن فعل (الإتيان) تكرر في النمل اثنتي عشرة مرة. وتكرر في القصص ست مرات فناسب تكرار {آتِيكُمْ} في النمل من كل وجه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A shihāb is a bright, shining flame; a qabas is a flame taken from a larger fire, and the root also describes acquiring knowledge.
rows.anchor: فذكر في سورة النمل أنه يأتيهم بشهاب قبس، والشهاب: هو شعلة من النار ساطعة. ومعنى (القَبَس) شعلة نار تقتبس من معظم النار

rows.speaker: أبيّ بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb says that the trust includes a woman being entrusted to guard her chastity.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال أبيّ بن كعب: من الأمانة أن اؤتمنت المرأةُ على فَرْجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith calls the muezzin entrusted, meaning people entrust him with their prayers and fasting.
rows.anchor: يعني: أن المؤذن أمينُ الناس على صلاتهم وصيامهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith that gatherings are a trust is taken as a call not to repeat what was said or done in a gathering; what one hears or sees there is entrusted to one.
rows.anchor: إلى تركِ إعادة ما يجري في المجلس من قولٍ أو فعل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amanah can refer to obedience, worship, a deposit, trustworthiness, or security, with hadith reports associated with these senses.
rows.anchor: والأمانة تقع على الطاعة والعبادة والوديعة والثقة والأمان، وقد جاء في كل منها حديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says faith is a trust and there is no faith or religion for someone without trustworthiness.
rows.anchor: الإيمانُ أمانة ولا دِينَ لمن لا أمانةَ له". وفي حديث آخر: "لا إيمان لمن لا أمانة له".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the supplication entrusting a person’s religion and amāna to God, amāna is explained as family, dependents left behind, and entrusted property.
rows.anchor: أي: أهلك، ومَنْ تخلفه بعدك منهم، ومالك الذي تودعه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority of commentators take trusts and covenants broadly: duties from God and people, including religious obligations, deposits, oaths, vows, and contracts.
rows.anchor: الآية عند أكثر المفسرين عامة في كل ما ائتُمِنُوا عليه، وعوهدوا من جهة الله تعالى، ومن جهة الناس

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: Rūḥ al-Maʿānī reports that amānāt is plural because trusts are numerous and varied for each person, whereas ʿahd is singular because it is less numerous or because it is a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وكأنه لكثرة الأمانة، جُمعت ولم يُجمع العهدُ، قيل: إيذاناً بأنه ليس كالأمانة كثرة، وقيل: لأنه مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The traits surrounding the protection of chastity are a remedy for haluʿ: resisting desire trains a person to be patient instead of rushing after every tempting opportunity.
rows.anchor: هذه الآيات مرتبطةٌ بما قبلها أجمل ارتباط. وهي مع ما ذُكِرَ معها من الأوصاف مَنْجاةٌ من الهلع وعلاج له.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guarding chastity and limiting sexual access to its lawful recipients is more important than guarding and hoarding wealth while withholding what is due to its recipients.
rows.anchor: هذا من ناحية، ومن ناحية ثانية إن حفظ الفروج وعدم إرسالها إلا على مستحقيها، أولى من حِفْظِ المال وكنزه ومنع مستحقه منه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keeping trusts and covenants can cost one protection from powerful people or a major immediate benefit; patiently fulfilling them and seeking God’s reward weakens the haluʿ disposition.
rows.anchor: وهذا علاج للهلع أيضاً، ذلك أن الأمانة والعهد ربما يُلْحِقان بالمؤتمن ضرراً من سلطة أو متنفِّذ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that 23:63 says their hearts are submerged, unlike 51:11 which says they are in a state of heedlessness; naming hearts matters because the heart is the locus of humility and cannot be humble while engulfed.
rows.anchor: كما قال في مكان آخر من القرآن الكريم (الذاريات 11) بل قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people who give what they give while fearing their return to God have hearts marked by awe, a quality associated with humility; the disbelievers’ submerged hearts prevent it.
rows.anchor: والوجَلُ أمرٌ قلبي وهو من لوازم الخشوع أيضاً. وذكرُ الكفار وذمهم بقوله: {بَلْ قُلُوبُهُمْ فِي غَمْرَةٍ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their failure to submit or supplicate to their Lord means they lack humility, since the humble person is submissive, pleading, and abject before God.
rows.anchor: فلم يخشعوا، لأن الخاشع مستكين لربه متضرع متذلل إليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arrogance and being high-handed contradict humility, which consists of lowering oneself and submitting to God.
rows.anchor: وقال: {فاستكبروا وَكَانُواْ قَوْماً عَالِينَ} والاستكبارُ والعُلوُّ مناقضان للخشوع، إذ الخشوع، تَطَامنٌ وتَذلُّلٌ وخضوعٌ لله رب العالمين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning al-Muʾminūn with humility suits the sūra’s atmosphere, and it begins with the quality reported to disappear first and ends with prayer, reported to disappear last.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بما يُرفع أولاً، وختم بما يرفع آخراً، وهو الصلاة،

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
rows.claim: ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit says that a time will soon come when one enters the mosque and sees no man there who is humble.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء عن عبادة بن الصامت أنه قال: "يوشك أن تدخل المسجد، فلا ترى فيه رجلاً خاشعاً".

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Ḥudhayfa says humility will be the first thing lost from religion and prayer the last, as Islam’s bonds are undone one by one.
rows.anchor: وعن حذيفة أنه قال: "أولُ ما تَفقدون من دينكم الخشوع، وآخرُ ما تفقدون من دينكم الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author observes that the descriptions in al-Muʾminūn and al-Maʿārij are strongly parallel but also differ in wording and order.
rows.anchor: هناك تشابه كبير بين النصين، كما أن هناك اختلافاً بينهما كما هو ظاهر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muʾminūn describes believers as humble in prayer, while al-Maʿārij describes them as constant in prayer; the author opens a comparison of these distinct descriptions.
rows.anchor: وقال في سورة المعارج: {الذين هُمْ على صَلاَتِهِمْ دَآئِمُونَ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separating pronoun and definite predicate restrict true inheritance to those who gather the stated qualities; the next clause explains that they inherit Firdaws, and the ambiguity followed by clarification adds grandeur.
rows.anchor: فجاء بضمير الفصل والتعريف في الخبر، للدلالة على القصر، أي: هؤلاء الجامعون لهذه الأوصاف، هم الوارثون الحقيقيون وليس غيرهم.

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf says these people alone deserve the name heirs and that the following Firdaws clause translates the identity of the heirs with striking majesty.
rows.anchor: جاء في (الكشاف) : " (أولئك) الجامعون لهذه الأوصاف (هم الوارثون) الأحقّاء بأن يُسَمّوا وُرّاثاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting fīhā signals restriction and mirrors earlier fronted descriptions; those who confined their deeds to good are rewarded with lasting only in Firdaws, the highest and best Garden.
rows.anchor: ثم انظر إلى تقديم الجار والمجرور على الخبر، في قوله: {هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ} للدلالة على القصر وتناسب ذلك مع التقديم في الأوصاف السابقة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author identifies Firdaws as the highest and best Garden, from which the rivers of Paradise flow, citing a hadith.
rows.anchor: والفردوس أعلى الجنة وأفضلها ومنه تتفجر أنهار الجنة كما جاء في الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning with harm is appropriate to the sūra’s opening demand for punishment and its atmosphere; panic also contrasts with the command to the Prophet to be patient with beautiful patience.
rows.anchor: وذِكْرُ الجزع ههنا وهو عدم الصبر مناسب لقوله تعالى في أوائل السورة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception of those who pray removes them from both sides of haluʿ: panic when harm comes and withholding when good comes.
rows.anchor: واستثنى من الاتصاف بصفة الهلع هذه بشقيها: الجزع والمنع للخير، مَن ذكرَهم بعد هذه الآية بقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawām in prayer means regular, attentive observance through its completion without distraction, not praying continuously at all times.
rows.anchor: والدوام على الصلاة معناه المواظبةُ عليها والانهماكُ فيها حتى تنتهي، وعدم الانشغال عنها، وليس المراد أنهم يصلون أبداً.

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority cited in al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ understand constancy in prayer as regular observance.
rows.anchor: جاء في (البحر المحيط) : "ديمومتها، قال الجمهور: المواظبة عليها.

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd explains constancy as praying at the prescribed time.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: صلاتها لوقتها.

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir explains constancy as praying calmly without turning to the right or left.
rows.anchor: وقال عقبة بن عامر: يقرّون فيها ولا يلتفتون يميناً ولا شمالاً

rows.speaker: فتح القدير
rows.claim: Fatḥ al-Qadīr says nothing distracts or diverts them from prayer, and that the phrase does not mean praying perpetually.
rows.anchor: وجاء في (فتح القدير) : "أي لا يَشغلهم عنها شاغل، ولا يصرفهم عنها صارف، وليس المراد بالدوام أنهم يصلّون أبداً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persistent prayer treats panic by cultivating continuous patience; people often pray but fail to maintain attention because their thoughts and distractions take much of the prayer away.
rows.anchor: فالدوام عليها علاج من أنجع الأدوية للتعويد على الصبر والمعافاة من الجزع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persistent prayer also treats withholding: a worshipper gives God the self and time, and learns freedom from desires even when worship brings no obvious worldly gain or costs an immediate opportunity.
rows.anchor: ذلك أن الدائم في صلاته يتعود أن يُعطي من نفسه ووقته لربه، بل يعطيه نَفْسَهُ كُلَّها ووقته في الصلاة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the passage did not stop at the general label those who pray, but specified those who persist in their prayers because persistence is the therapeutic quality.
rows.anchor: ولذا لم يكتف بقوله {إِلاَّ المصلين} بل قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the known due in their wealth as zakat because its amount is fixed and known; another view takes it otherwise, without further detail here.
rows.anchor: قيل: إن المراد بالحق المعلوم الزكاة لأنها مُقَدَّرةٌ معلومة، وقيل: غير ذلك.
